standard_text: Viruses, bacteria, protists and fungi: their general structure and the role they play in ecosystems; diseases they cause (HIV/AIDS, cholera, tuberculosis, malaria, thrush); the immune response; the use of micro-organisms in biotechnology. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 11, Life Sciences: Biodiversity of micro-organisms)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): viruses, bacteria, protists and fungi, the diseases they cause, immunity and useful micro-organisms. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Viruses can only reproduce inside living cells.
body_html:
How to think about it

Viruses are not cells: they have a protein coat around DNA or RNA and reproduce only inside host cells. Bacteria are prokaryotic cells without a nucleus. Protists are single-celled eukaryotes, such as the Plasmodium that causes malaria. Fungi include yeasts and moulds.

Micro-organisms are decomposers, nitrogen fixers and are used to make bread, yoghurt and medicines. Some cause disease: HIV (a virus) attacks the immune system; tuberculosis and cholera are bacterial diseases; malaria is caused by a protist carried by mosquitoes.

Example

Can antibiotics cure flu?

Flu is caused by a virus.

Answer: no

Example

Which kind of organism causes malaria?

Plasmodium

Answer: a protist

Common mistakes

  • Thinking viruses are bacteria.
  • Thinking all micro-organisms are harmful.
  • Thinking malaria is spread by contaminated water.

items.q: What is passive immunity?

items.q: What do cytotoxic T cells do?

items.q: What is an autoimmune disease?

items.q: What is an antibody?
